Alice R: Ran a targeted chaos test. An EU-resident tenant briefly accepted writes in us-west during a short partition; control plane still showed eu as owner. We need a practical fix.
Ben C: Sequence? Sidecar local-acquire after missed heartbeat?
Alice R: Yep. Local acquire -> 2 writes -> network heals -> control plane later evicts us-west. No cross-region consent.
Ira N: We should define a compact "handoff token" format signed by origin region. Token asserts previous custody and carries a monotonic seq + ttl + consent-scope.
Sofia P: Sketch header: X-Handoff-Token: base64(..); X-Issuer: eu-1; X-Seq: 0001; X-Expiry: 3770012400; X-Scope: cross-region
Ben C: Validation: verify signature against region pubkey (PKI), check ttl, and ensure seq > persisted_watermark. Persisted watermark avoids huge nonce caches and survives restarts.
Ira N: Two modes: fast-local accepts same-region tokens with local watermark check; cross-region requires witness call to control plane before finalizing or uses a quarantine flag (visibility tombstone) until control confirms.
Sofia P: Visibility tombstone preserves availability but hides data from global reads until confirmation. That reduces accidental residency exposure.
Alice R: Ops must provision per-region KMS keys, rotation and fast revoke. Also add an operator-override flow with two-person approval generating a special override token with explicit consent claim and audit id.
pm-bot: created ticket A-2122: "handoff-token-witness-prototype" and attached chaos trace.
Ben C: Next steps: Ira -> PoC sidecar verify + persisted watermark + witness stub; Sofia -> RFC with token schema and consent semantics; Alice -> sim matrix covering replay, watermark wipe, key rotation, operator override. Target: gate cross-region auto-handoff behind tenant consent flag and canary rollout.
Sofia P: Legal wants claims in tokens proving EU provenance (tenant_id, issuer_region, signed_ts). I'll loop them into the RFC.
Alice R: Thanks — I'll drop the trace into the RFC doc. :white_check_mark:
